claims.text: The Silsila weighs how hard a kill is against an amount and quality of vitae as the fee; the blood goes to a sorcerer who stores it for the Clan.
An assassin tithes ten percent of every payment to the sire and another ten percent to the Clan.
Brujah sort themselves by three loose outlooks, Iconoclast, Idealist and Individualist, which are neither political groups nor fixed; surviving Iconoclasts often become Individualists or Idealists.

title: The Lionesses of Sekhmet
summary: A Setite Gehenna cult inside the Camarilla.

claims.text: Early in the twentieth century a coterie of female Setites played on Camarilla women's anger at mostly male Princes, taking the mask of Sekhmet.
They dressed the Revelations of the Void as a path to an inner Lioness Power and run a Gehenna cult that eats at the Camarilla from inside.
The Lycaon line of Gangrel is dying out, and the Coyotes are the new blood; once mostly Sabbat, they have grown more common in recent decades and a few have sought the Camarilla.
Even an ordinary, mostly ignorant Giovanni household honours its ancestors and makes offerings to spirits.

title: Friends of the Night
summary: The hidden council of the Lasombra.

claims.text: A self-appointed group at the heart of the Lasombra, called in other ages the Amici Noctis or Amies Noires, steers the Clan from the shadows.
It wants the Clan to advance and adapt, but only in the way it chooses, and has the power to enforce that.
Most Nosferatu believe a band of ancient, powerful elders hunts their Clan to destroy every member.
Accounts differ: some call the Nictuku mindless monsters, others patient killers picking off Nosferatu one by one, but all agree they are deadly.
Svadharma is a Ravnos's own duty to better the self and the world, known by a revelation of purpose; it is rarely finished in one lifetime.
After the Embrace, returning to mortal life or posing as mortal is forbidden, as that is no longer the Ravnos's duty.

title: Toreador and Mortals
summary: Why the Clan stays among the living.

claims.text: Most Toreador keep a steady presence in mortal society and find mortals more genuine and surprising than Kindred.
The Clan has seven titles: Acolyte, Apprentice, Magister, Regent, Pontifex, Lord and Councilor.

A Regent masters a whole chantry and often leads the city's Tremere; Lords oversee several chantries over a region the size of a US state, and Pontifices rule countries, usually seven Lords to each of the seven Pontifices.
The Fiends aspire to what the dragon stands for, transformation, and seek the transcendent along the coils of Azi Dahaka.
A Ventrue's feeding restriction changes only through a great act of will after a hunger frenzy or torpor, most often after torpor from lack of vitae.
Caitiff can turn others' contempt into surprise, and learning many abilities free of Clan limits makes them versatile, above all in a fight.
Groups of Caitiff tend to be scattered, a coterie for safety or a loose political movement.
The Pander stand beside the two founding Clans as one of the few Sabbat groups not defined by opposing others, and resent being taken for ordinary Caitiff.
The Followers of Set have worshipped the serpent for thousands of years; the Serpents of the Light are their Sabbat antitribu.
An Assamite of the Ninth Generation, Embraced in 1867 by Ma'aruf, and of the same lineage as the notorious Fatima.
A Gangrel antitribu of the Twelfth Generation, Embraced in 1991 by Pedro Diaz, raised in Arkansas farm country.
A Brujah of the Fifth Generation, Embraced in 423 BCE by Menele, one of the Camarilla's oldest elders, now pushing the Sect to be more assertive.
A Giovanni of the Tenth Generation, Embraced in 1887 by Rosario Giovanni.
A Toreador of the Ninth Generation, Embraced in 1229 by Maiselle of Rochester, born in the village of Strood.
A Malkavian of the Seventh Generation, Embraced in 1915 by Trimeggian, born into wealth.
A Nosferatu antitribu of the Seventh Generation, Embraced in 1467 by Boronisk, once an officer in the army of Ivan the Great.
A Tzimisce of the Tenth Generation, Embraced in 1943 by Efrain Sortano, once a medical professor.
A Follower of Set of the Sixth Generation, Embraced in 532 by Khay'tall, founder of the cult called the Children of Judas.
Sarrasine flattered the Ventrue Prince Abram into the hubris of claiming all Australia, saw Abram overthrown and took the throne.
Sydney has long been a free city open to any vampire, but the court has grown decadent, and advisers such as the childe Ella Littleton question the lax rule.
A Ravnos of the Eighth Generation, Embraced in 1764 by Vasily Vasilevich, born to a noble family.
A Lasombra of the Eighth Generation, Embraced in 1957 by Tobias Smith as part of a Sabbat campaign.
A Tremere of the Ninth Generation, Embraced in 1950 by Duke Traska; a decorated Second World War soldier who later worked for an unnamed intelligence agency.
A Ventrue antitribu of the Ninth Generation, Embraced in 1327 by Leander Phipps, once a Templar in the Crusades.
